la:adj:vectigalis.html:
vectīgālis, e,
adj [id.].
Of or belonging to imposts or taxes: pecunia,i. e. impost, tribute,, cf.: annuum tributum,.—
Paying tribute, subject to imposts, tributary: civitas,: agri,, § 103: hos Suevi ... vectigales sibi fecerunt,; ; cf.: (Hannibal) vectigalis stipendiariusque et servus populi Romani,.—
Of or belonging to the revenue, that brings in revenue or income: equos vectigales tradere,: ita ei lecti sui contumelia vectigalis est,: libertas,: quadrigae, Ascon. ap. Bait.

la:noun:vectigal.html:
vectīgal, ālis (
gen. plur. vectigaliorum, ; : vectigalium,), n.
vectus, from veho
, a toll, tax, impost paid to the State (cf.: tributum, census, stipendium).
Lit.: in vectigalibus non solum adventus mali, sed etiam metus ipse affert calamitatem ... ita neque ex portu neque ex decumis neque ex scripturā vectigal conservari potest,; C. Gracch. ap. Gell 11, 10, 3; ; ; : pensitare,: imponere agro,: levare agrum vectigali,.—
Esp., an honorarium or contribution paid to a magistrate: praetorium,: aedilicium, the contribution of a province to the games instituted by an œdile, id. Q. Fr, 1, 1, 9, § 26.—
Transf, of private affairs, revenue, rents, income, etc.: vectigalia urbana rusticis (anteponantur),; cf.: ex meo tenui vectigali,; ; Col. praef. § 27; ; ; —Prov.: magnum vectigal est Parsimonia,.

la:noun:vectura.html:
vectūra, ae, f.
veho
,
a bearing, carrying, conveying, transportation by carriage or by ship; a riding, etc.
Lit. (class.): equi idonei ad vecturam,: misimus qui pro vecturā solveret,for the transportation,: mercium. : sine vecturae periculo. of transportation by sea, .— Plur.: remiges, arma, frumenta, vecturae imperabantur,transport, conveyance,: vecturas frumenti finitimis civitatibus descripsit,: onerum,.—
Transf., passage-money, freight-money, fare, freight, ; ; .

la:noun:vectis.html:
Vectis, is, f.,
an island south of Britain, now the Isle of Wight, ; .—Also called Vec-ta, f., Eutr 7, 19.

la:verb:vecto.html:
vecto, āvi, ātum, 1,
v. freq. a [veho], to bear, carry, convey (perh. not ante-Aug.): delphinum dorso super fluctus edito vectavisse (Arionem),: corpora viva nefas Stygiā vectare carinā,: plaustris ornos,: saucia corpora vectet aquā, (4, 2), 46; cf. v. 39.—Pass., to be carried or borne, to ride: vectabor umeris,: vectari equis,to ride on horseback,; ; : octophoro, App Mag. p. 323.

la:adj:vecors.html:
vē-cors (vāecors), cordis, adj.
cor
,
destitute of reason; senseless, silly, foolish;mad, insane (syn.: excors, delirus, vesanus): aliis cor ipsum animus videtur: ex quo excordes, vaecordes concordesque dicuntur,; cf.: vecors est turbati et mali cordis, Müll.: ego te non vaecordem, non furiosum, non mente captum, non tragico illo Oreste dementiorem putem?; ; ; ; : scelere et metu vecors,: pavidi vecordesque in primam pugnantium aciem procurrunt,; also: deformis habitu more vecordium in publicum evolat,: mens,: impetus prope vecors,: pertinacia,.—Comp.: vecordior,med.—Sup.: istius vaecordissimi mentem terrebant,; .

la:noun:vector.html:
vector, ōris, m.
veho
.
Act., one that bears, carries, or conveys any thing; a bearer, carrier (poet. and in post-Aug. prose); (equus) gradarius optimu' vector, Lucil. ap. : Sileni (asellus),: puellae (taurus),: stelligeri Olympi (Atlas),: vector meus,i. e. my horse,; , p. 140.—
Neutr., one that rides upon any thing; a rider, traveller, passenger (class.); on a ship: etiam summi gubernatores in magnis tempestatibus a vectoribus admoneri solent,: ingratis vectoribus bene gubernare,; ; ; : animosius a mercatore quam a vectore solvitur votum,; ; ; — In mal. part.: numquam nisi navi plenā tollo vectorem, Macr S. 2, 5.—On horseback, a rider, horseman: vector equum regit, Ov A. A. 3, 555; .
